classification.difficultyReason: Choose the opposing triangles around E, derive equal sides from the midpoint givens, and connect parallel-line and vertically opposite angles to AAS congruence before concluding AE=EC.

content.prompt: In the parallelogram $ABCD$, $F$ is the midpoint of $AD$ and $G$ is the midpoint of $BC$. If $AC$ and $FG$ intersect at $E$, prove that $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$.

spec.description: Parallelogram with diagonal AC and midpoint connector FG meeting at E; matching single and double parallel arrows retained. Ordinary source blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel DC; AD parallel BC; F on AD; G on BC; A,E,C collinear; F,E,G collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and labels are visible.

answer.short:
$AE=EC$, so $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$.

Use $\triangle AEF\equiv\triangle CEG$ (AAS).
answer.worked:
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so $AD=BC$. Since $F$ and $G$ are midpoints, $AF=CG$.

In triangles $AEF$ and $CEG$:
$$\begin{align*}
AF&=CG &&\text{(halves of equal sides)}\\
\angle FAE&=\angle GCE &&\text{(alternate angles, }AD\parallel BC\text{)}\\
\angle AEF&=\angle CEG &&\text{(vertically opposite angles).}
\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle AEF\equiv\triangle CEG$ (AAS), so $AE=EC$ (matching sides). Since $E$ lies on $AC$, $E$ is its midpoint.
